messages:
Amanda: quick sims attached — ran 10k-request trace with realistic mix (short chats 65%, long-context 25%, embeddings 10%). baseline = 120 GPUs (A100 equiv).
Amanda: p95 = 185ms, p99 = 620ms, avg queue length 2.1, 90th GPU utilization = 78%.
Ryan: can you paste the arrival distribution and service-time assumptions?
Amanda: arrival: Poisson lambda=140 req/s peak (trace-derived). service times: short=40ms, medium=180ms, long=700ms tail (we use pareto k=1.3 for long requests).
Liam: thanks. so long-tail requests dominate p99, unsurprising. what's the admission policy in the sim?
Amanda: soft admit curve: allow until per-GPU queue depth 3, then prob. admit drops linearly to 0 at depth 8. also fallback to small-model for admitted drop.
Maria: what happens if we instead hard-admit at depth 5? numbers?
Amanda: hard-admit @5 -> p95 200ms, p99 730ms, dropped requests 4.6%. cost same.
Ryan: and adding capacity? say +20 GPUs (to 140)?
Amanda: +20 GPUs -> p95 170ms, p99 420ms, avg queue 1.4, 90th util 67%. cost delta ~ $1.6k/day (onsite pricing estimated).
Liam: so tradeoff is approx $1.6k/day to pull p99 down ~300ms. Is that acceptable for prod SLO?
Maria: Our SLO is p95 <200ms, p99 <500ms. +20 GPUs would put us below both. Hard-admit can't. soft-admit + fallback also meets SLO at 120 GPUs? looks close but p99 is 620ms so no.
Amanda: right. another lever: more aggressive fallback (route 40% of long-context to smaller model) at 120 GPUs -> p99 470ms, p95 190ms, user-visible quality drop TBD.
Ryan: do we have metrics on user quality loss for that fallback? eval set?
Amanda: quick eval on 5k prompts shows ROUGE down ~3.2 points for long-context when using small-model. we'll run more later.
Liam: propose three options for leadership: 1) +20 GPUs (preserve quality, cost +$1.6k/day) 2) keep capacity + soft fallback (quality drop ~3pts, no infra cost) 3) hybrid: +10 GPUs + 20% fallback -> p99 ~490ms, p95 175ms, cost +$0.8k/day.
Maria: leaning to option 3. can we simulate seasonal spike +40% (holiday week) and see headroom?
Amanda: ran that: with +10 GPUs +20% fallback under +40% arrivals -> p95 220ms, p99 710ms (fails). +20 GPUs option holds: p95 185ms, p99 490ms under spike.
capacity-bot: forecast uploaded: "holiday-week" spike +40% expected Dec 14-21. reserved capacity lead time 3-4 weeks.
Ryan: ops question — procurement timeline ok for +20 GPUs?
Maria: procurement + infra setup takes ~3 weeks if we approve today.
Liam: risk: long-tail requests may increase with newer multimodal models. prefer capacity + some fallback.
Amanda: recommendation in doc: approve +10 GPUs now, enable 20% fallback as temporary safety, re-evaluate after two weeks of telemetry. if forecast spikes firm, approve +20 GPUs.
Maria: +1 to Amanda's plan. Ryan, can you draft the procurement request?
Ryan: on it. will attach sim outputs and cost table.
Amanda: attaching command I used for sims:
Amanda: ```
./simulate_capacity --gpus 120 --trace traces/production_apr.trace 
  --arrival-scale 1.0 --fallback-rate 0.0 --admit "soft:3-8" 
./simulate_capacity --gpus 140 --arrival-scale 1.0 --fallback-rate 0.0 --admit "soft:3-8"
./simulate_capacity --gpus 120 --arrival-scale 1.0 --fallback-rate 0.4 --admit "soft:3-8"
./simulate_capacity --gpus 130 --arrival-scale 1.4 --fallback-rate 0.2 --admit "soft:3-8"
```
Liam: will add a quick sensitivity table to the PR.
Maria: thanks all. next steps: Ryan opens procurement ticket, Amanda posts updated sims in #eng-sre in 24h, enable feature-flagged fallback ramp to 20% for next 48h.
Ryan: filed ticket INC-7849 and linked this thread.
Amanda: noted, I'll ramp fallback and monitor p99, error budget burn. :eyes:
Maria: closing loop — great work, that plan sounds balanced. :thumbsup:
